findings.claim: A real sensor's internally filtered output can be fused downstream as white noise
findings.value: not established: the correlation shown is that of a declared synthetic filter; a real sensor's internal filter is unknown here

hypothesis: Filtered estimates are correlated in time even when the sensor noise is white; the steady-state correlation is [(I - K H) F]^j P, and ignoring it underestimates the variance of averaged filter outputs.
input_data: scalar: 20000 runs x 30 ticks from the steady state
planar CV: 4000 runs from P_ss, camera R, dt = 0.1 s, q = 0.05
mathematical_model: e_{k+1} = (I - K H) F e_k + (I - K H) w_k - K v_{k+1} in steady state gives Cov(e_{k+j}, e_k) = A^j P with A = (I - K H) F. Scalar random walk: q = 1, r = 30, M^2 = qM + qr -> M = 6, P = 5, K = 1/6, a = 5/6; Var(mean of n) = P/n^2 [n + 2 sum_j (n - j) a^j]. Innovations of the optimal filter are white.
numerical_result: V_20 / (P/20) = 8.078; naive 95% interval coverage 0.510 (Monte Carlo 0.507); scalar autocovariance max |z| 1.43; planar max |z| 1.59 vs 4.39; lag-1 position error correlation 0.869.
observation_model: Scalar z = x + v, v ~ N(0, 30); planar z = (px, py) + v, v ~ N(0, R_camera).
